Q: How do ETL, ELT and incremental updates change where failures are repaired?
spoken: ETL transforms before loading the destination, while ELT loads a retained representation before downstream transformation. Incremental processing changes only new or modified source state under a cursor or change contract. Choose from data volume, governance, latency and rebuild requirements; the acronym does not supply deduplication or correctness guarantees.

Q: Why must a CDC checkpoint and destination state have a recovery contract?
spoken: A checkpoint that advances before the destination is durable can lose an update. A destination commit before acknowledgment can cause redelivery after a crash. Use an atomic local checkpoint with projection writes when possible and payload-bound receipts or idempotent destination operations for replay. State the source-partition scope of the guarantee.
A:
A checkpoint that advances before the destination is durable can lose an update. A destination commit before acknowledgment can cause redelivery after a crash. Use an atomic local checkpoint with projection writes when possible and payload-bound receipts or idempotent destination operations for replay. State the source-partition scope of the guarantee.

Q: How should data-quality quarantine avoid silently losing or exposing records?
spoken: Declare which violations stop processing and which are quarantined while progress continues. Retain safe reason codes, source identity and repair provenance without copying sensitive bodies into unrestricted logs. Track quarantine counts and age so the system cannot appear healthy while excluding a growing slice of source data.
